steps.text: Preheat the oven to 350 degrees F (175 degrees C).

In an 8x8-inch square pan, stir together flour, white sugar, 1/4 cup of cocoa, baking powder, and salt. Add milk and oil; mix well. Sprinkle brown sugar, remaining cocoa, and chocolate chips over mixture. Add vanilla to hot water, then pour water over top of mixture.
Bake for 30 to 35 minutes in the preheated oven, until surface appears dry. Serve warm with a spoon or at room temperature.

raw_recipe.headline: Chocolate Pudding Cake
raw_recipe.description: A delicious, easy pudding cake, wonderful served warm with a spoonful of whipped cream. Try mint chocolate chips for a change.

review.reviewBody: Wow--Five stars with the following changes: 1/2 cup each brown & white sugar instead of the 2/3 cup. Instead of the hot water, use very hot HALF & HALF with 2 teaspoons vanilla. This gives a MUCH creamier pudding and won't taste like a cake of flour and water, like some have said of this type of recipe. I've made it both ways and I can't believe how much better the recipe with half and half is!!! Why has no one published a recipe like this?!!! :-)

After a recent dinner out my husband became obsessed with the chocolate pudding cake we had for dessert. So I thought I'd see if I could make it at home. I must admit I was a little skeptical of how this would turn out when I decided to give it a go. My skepticism was all for naught! This is a FABULOUS dessert! It's so easy, and so good there is no reason not to make this every single day!!! ;) Seriously though, my husband was floored. He told me that mine was better than restaurant version! He was very happy! I made it for a recent get together and the hostess asked if I had gotten it at a local bakery that always has huge lines. She was shocked that this wonderful dessert came from my own kitchen! She said "It seems like it would be SO complicated!" Little does she know it's a SNAP!! Seriously folks, if you want to please and delight the chocolate lovers in your life, make them this chocolate pudding cake! They will thank you! As for the recipe, I also did a 1/2 cup of white and brown sugar instead of the 2/3 cup. The cake was plenty sweet and very decadent. I baked it for 30 minutes and let it set for about 20 minutes more. It was warm and gooey and amazing! LOVE THIS!!

Divine chocolate pudding cake! Aside from measuring cups and spoons, all you dirty up is a whisk to mix, and the pan you bake in! I made a small addition to the ingredients. Instead of 1 1/4 cup hot water, I microwaved 1 1/4 cup of whole milk (about 1:30 minutes depending on microwave wattage) and then added 3 tablespoons espresso powder to the hot milk + the vanilla. The espresso brings out the chocolate taste MUCH more, and the milk gives the "pudding" a creamier, silky texture. DELICIOUS!

This is a delicious pudding cake. I used 1/2 c. white sugar and 2/3 c. brown sugar. Also added 2 tsp. instant coffee with the vanilla to the hot water. I made a pudding cake years ago that boiled over so I put my 9" pan on a cookie sheet just in case. It didn't even come close to boiling over. I baked it for 29 min....turned out delish(or did I already say that?)

Substituted instant unsweetened vanilla pudding mix for the 1/4 cup cocoa in the dry ingredients, and increases the milk to 170 ml. In the last step, added the vanilla extract to hot milk instead of to water. Increased baking time to 55 mins. Will make this many more times!

This was sooooo good. I messed it up as I was making it and it still tasted fabulous. Didn't read the recipe all the way through and added all the cocoa powder at once, so I just added a 1/4 more at the end. Also subbed some half and half and water for the water. It made it rich and creamy like a real pudding bottom. Let it sit for about 30 minutes before eating too. I think this helped the sauce thicken up. Had it with some coffee ice cream. It was bliss!!

This is a great recipe as it is but if you want to kick it up substitute the hot water with hot coffee. Mix 1 egg yolk into the batter for extra creamy richness. Wip the egg white into medium stiff peaks and fold into batter then place chocolate chips on top of batter, next brown sugar, followed by hot coffee & vanilla. Bake as directed. It should rise and crisp a bit on the edges and still be gooey and delish!

I just made this in an 8 inch round cake pan and it was delicious! Most of the time I hate chocolate but there are some rare odd times when I absolutely crave it, had one of those this morning so upon browsing this site came across this recipe. Already had all the ingredients on hand so decided to try it. I have no clue how the liquid mixture sinks down to the bottom upon baking but it somehow does and mine came out to be a liquid (kind of a cross between a syrup and a pudding) chocolaty amazing concoction on the bottom and a divine brownie on top. Anyway make sure that you do not stir the liquid in after pouring it on top as you're not supposed to. Just take it straight to the oven after pouring the water on top. The only things that I really changed was added some almond extract in with the vanilla extract in the hot water, and I only had like a half of a handful of Chocolate Chunks from the last time I made CC Cookies so not thinking that was enough for me, I took 8 melting centers hershey's kisses and put that on top along with the brown sugar/coca powder mixture. The only change I made other than these slight changes was I decreased the brown sugar TO 1/2 of a cup. It's plenty sweet like that, in fact I might decrease the white sugar to that amount next time as well. Would be perfect with vanilla ice cream although I only had mine with whipped cream this first time. Now excuse me while I go get myself another bowl of this deliciousness!!

This is so easy to make and so versatile. The first time I made it, I made true to this recipe. Now we throw in peanut butter or butterscotch chips, I sometimes don't use any chips. I've thrown in toasted coconut, roasted and chopped pecans. The 2 things I always do now is use butter instead of oil and milk instead of water. Go out on a limb and put instant espresso in the hot milk before pouring over the cake mix. It adds a LOADS of flavor and richness. Great recipe and super easy

Just as fantastic as everyone says plus fat free yippee! I wanted to add that I've scaled the recipe down to 4 servings and cooked it in a large microwavable mug around 1- 1.5 minutes I think? Use a deep mug because it will rise up and bubble and use a toothpick to check done-ness but it's worked for me several times and it's much better than the microwave chocolate mug cake! Be sure to let it sit a bit afterwards because it's super hot. Also it's the perfect serving size when it's just my boyfriend and I.
This was great. I replaced 1 cup of hot water with 1 cup of hot half and half. It’s a good cross between cake and brownie. Whole house loved it.
I added two eggs for depth.
My mom made this when I was a little girl. Has always been a favorite!
Put 1/2 cup brown sugar & 1/2 cup white sugar & instead of water, I used very hot half & half with vanilla suggested by Full Time Mom. Much better

Don’t mix in the square pan. It is more trouble than it is worth. Just mix the batter in a mixing bowl and add to the square pan, sprinkle the chocolate chips. Then combine the brown sugar, hot water and vanilla in a small bowl and pour over the batter as directed in the recipe. The operations outlined in recipe take a lot of extra time and don’t account for the fact brown sugar is often hard unless you have stored it carefully.
So easy. A had a chocolate craving. I never made a pudding cake. This was done quickly and perfect. I'll add nuts next time. Like a gooey brownie with whipped cream.

This is one of those recipes you don't judge by what it looks like in the pan. Served warm with a bit of whipped topping makes up for its lackluster appearance however. I added extra miniature chocolate chips so that nearly every other bite had a bit of texture. An easy treat!
Quick easy and amazing warm or room temperature. Goes great with your favorite ice cream!!!

I’m sad to have to side with the bland reviews….it’s not bad, definitely not indulgent or decadent with flavor…it’s a fun dessert in its own rights. It smells Great but the flavor is just not there…I even subbed half the water for milk and used butter instead of oil….my kids like it so I guess that’s all that matters
